meta.name: Open questions, missing information and what would have to be answered before a decision
meta.rule: Every row below is a question this system cannot yet answer from the information the repository holds. The 'what we have' column is evidence; the 'what we do not have' column is the gap; 'how to close it' names an official, checkable source. No row asserts a fact that has not been checked.

statusMeaning.open: Cannot be answered from current official data. Blocks at least one decision.
statusMeaning.blocked: Cannot be answered at all right now, because the official publisher has not published it.
statusMeaning.partial: Partially answerable; the remaining part is named in the gap column.
statusMeaning.answered: Answered in this session from an official source; link in the source column.

questions.question: Which official source publishes NFL point spreads, moneylines or totals that we are allowed to cite row by row?
questions.have: Nothing. nfl.com game pages, week pages and team stat pages were probed by exact regex (nfl/research/probe.json): odds/spread/moneyline field counts are all 0.
questions.gap: No official NFL price feed is available in this repository. Any price must therefore be typed in by the owner with the book, timestamp and screenshot, or the system publishes a model number and labels it MODEL — not a market line.
questions.howToClose: Decide whether to consume a licensed odds API under the owner's own account, or to record prices manually as observations. Both need a decision before any ROI claim is published.
questions.blocks: Every ROI, closing-line-value and price-outperformance claim.

questions.question: What does 'originating my own line' mean for this project: a fair-price model, or a tradable two-way price with a hold?
questions.have: The engine can produce win probabilities and devigged fair prices from any two-way price pair (functions implemented in nfl/tools/analyze_market.py and unit-tested).
questions.gap: The owner has not stated whether the published number must include a margin (juice) and, if so, whether it should be a fixed hold or a per-market hold.
questions.howToClose: One decision from the owner. Default proposed in nfl/curated/validation-gates.json: publish fair price and a suggested price at a stated hold.
questions.blocks: Presentation of the line, and the definition of a winning bet.

questions.question: How many settled bets are needed before a strategy may be called skill-based rather than lucky?
questions.have: A statistical gate is implemented (binomial test against the break-even probability implied by the price, plus a Monte-Carlo shuffle test that destroys any real edge).
questions.gap: The threshold is a policy choice, not a fact. The gate currently refuses to certify anything below 100 settled bets and reports the p-value so the owner can see how weak the evidence is.
questions.howToClose: Owner decision on the false-positive budget. Record it in nfl/curated/validation-gates.json before results accumulate, so the threshold cannot be moved after the fact.

questions.question: Are the rewards real money, an honour system, or a paper scoreboard?
questions.have: A leaderboard schema with scoring formulas (Brier score, log loss, ROI, closing-line value, calibration error) and a demotion/probation rule.
questions.gap: No reward currency, no payout rule and no eligibility rule exists. The site therefore publishes ranks only and states that no monetary reward is promised.
questions.howToClose: Owner decision. Until then the leaderboard is explicitly 'no reward, ranking only'.
questions.blocks: Any statement that a strategy 'earns' something.

questions.question: Does the official injury report tell us who will actually start?
questions.have: The NFL official report gives player, position, injury, practice status and game status (Out / Doubtful / Questionable) per team per week. 2026 weeks 1-10 and 2025 weeks 1-18 are loaded.
questions.gap: It does not name the replacement. 'Questionable' is not a probability. Practice status is not a snap count.
questions.howToClose: Join the injury report to each club's official depth chart (done) and to official snap-count/gamebook data (not yet loaded; see Q07).

questions.question: How deep is each defence and offence behind the listed starter — is the 2nd string a real drop-off or a coin flip?
questions.have: Official club depth charts give 1st/2nd/3rd/4th string at every position for each club that publishes one, with the club's own 'updated as of' date.
questions.gap: A depth chart is a projection by the club, not a performance measurement. Several clubs label theirs 'Unofficial Depth Chart'. Depth is not quality: the 2nd string is not always worse.
questions.howToClose: Replace the projection with measured performance of the actual participants (official snap counts and player stats). Until then the site shows depth as a flag, never as a rating.
questions.blocks: Quantifying 'deficiency' in a defence or offence.

questions.question: Which players actually played, and how many snaps?
questions.have: Nothing official in this repository yet. Player season stat pages publish per-game logs (WK, OPP, RESULT and stat columns) which imply participation.
questions.gap: No official snap-count feed is loaded. Absence from a game log is not proof of zero snaps — a player can play and record no stat.
questions.howToClose: Add the official NFL gamebook / snap-count publication as a source, or accept that participation is inferred from stat logs and label it as such.

questions.question: Which player props in the same game are positively correlated, and by how much?
questions.have: Official per-game player stat logs for the loaded seasons, which is exactly the input a correlation estimate needs.
questions.gap: The sample is small (a partial season), so any correlation estimate carries a wide confidence interval. Estimates are published with n and a bootstrap interval, and are withheld below n=8 games.
questions.howToClose: Accumulate more official game logs; resample with a block bootstrap; never publish a correlation without its interval.
questions.blocks: Parlay correlation adjustment and same-game parlay pricing.

questions.question: Do game-level outcomes correlate with the props inside them (e.g. a big favourite rushing more)?
questions.have: Final scores for every played 2025 and 2026 game, plus per-game player logs.
questions.gap: Mapping a player log row to a specific game requires the opponent and week to match the schedule; that join is implemented but only covers games where both official pages exist.
questions.howToClose: Complete the join and report the match rate. Unmatched rows are excluded and counted, never guessed.

questions.question: What is the minimum sample and the multiple-testing correction before a strategy is promoted?
questions.have: A gate list with explicit pass/fail logic, including a Benjamini-Hochberg style false-discovery guard when many strategies are tested at once.
questions.gap: The reward rule and the promotion threshold are policy, not fact. Defaults are proposed and marked as defaults.
questions.howToClose: Owner sign-off, recorded before results are seen.

questions.question: Is there enough history to backtest at all?
questions.have: 2025 and 2026 official results and player logs are loaded on demand by CI.
questions.gap: Two partial seasons with no historical prices is not a backtest of a betting strategy; it is a backtest of a probability model. Any strategy that needs prices cannot be backtested yet (see Q01).
questions.howToClose: Either obtain licensed historical prices, or restrict backtests to probability-scoring (Brier/log-loss) and label them 'no price backtest'.

questions.question: Are the depth charts the same thing across all 32 clubs?
questions.have: Per-club pages with per-club 'updated as of' dates and per-club naming (some say 'Unofficial').
questions.gap: They are not normalised: some clubs publish 4 tiers, some 3; some list 11 defensive positions, some 12. Cross-club comparison of 'depth' is therefore approximate and is flagged as such.
questions.howToClose: Publish a per-club chart schema note and never sum across clubs without saying so.

questions.question: Could a page change between two fetches in the same day?
questions.have: Every record carries the fetch time and the exact source URL it came from.
questions.gap: Yes — injury reports and depth charts change during the week, and week pages gain scores. The site therefore stamps each table with its retrieval time.
questions.howToClose: Re-run the CI fetch before publishing anything time-sensitive; the site shows the stamp so staleness is visible.
questions.blocks: Nothing, provided the stamp is shown.

questions.question: How do the two partial-season datasets compare in size and shape?
questions.have: Counts per dataset are published on the Data health page and in nfl/data/fetch-report.json.
questions.gap: Coverage is not completeness. A missing week page means missing games, not zero games; the report lists every failed fetch.
questions.howToClose: Read fetch-report.json failures before trusting any aggregate.

questions.question: What is the baseline every strategy must beat?
questions.have: Baselines defined: coin flip (50% ATS), home-field prior from official results, and the market's own devigged price when a price exists.
questions.gap: With no prices (Q01), the only baselines available are probability-scoring baselines, not ROI baselines.
questions.howToClose: State the baseline per competition in the strategy registry.

questions.question: How should rest, travel and short weeks be handled?
questions.have: Official kickoff dates and venues for every 2026 game, from which rest days can be derived exactly.
questions.gap: Travel distance is not published; deriving it means adding a venue-coordinate source, which is not an official NFL page.
questions.howToClose: Either drop travel, or publish it as an estimate with the non-official coordinate source named.

questions.question: Who reviews a suggestion, and what stops a suggestion contradicting a verified table?
questions.have: A suggestions register with status, owner, review gate and a check that a suggestion touching a verified row must cite its source.
questions.gap: No reviewer is assigned. The register therefore defaults every row to 'awaiting review' and nothing is auto-accepted.
questions.howToClose: Assign the reviewer role. Until then the Suggestion review page lists decisions in open state only.

questions.question: What happens when two strategies claim the same edge, or when a strategy's live results diverge from its backtest?
questions.have: A probation rule: a strategy whose live scoring diverges from its declared expectation by more than the stated tolerance is demoted to probation and its reward is withheld.
questions.gap: The tolerance value is a policy choice, not a fact.
questions.howToClose: Owner sets the tolerance in nfl/curated/validation-gates.json.
